A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D-NGD research. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the new Appendices A.11–A.12 in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original PINN training experiments on seven PDE benchmarks, with numerical errors in Table 1 and convergence curves in Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds primal-versus-dual timing measurements and preconditioner analyses in Appendices A.11–A.12.

M1.justification: The dual Gauss–Newton/Levenberg–Marquardt formulation, geodesic correction, dense solver, and Nyström-preconditioned CG procedure remain unchanged. Equations 6–11 and Algorithms 1–6 retain the same operations; the new complexity discussion does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The same seven PDE benchmarks remain. The added studies vary residual counts, parameter counts, and preconditioner ranks within Navier–Stokes/cavity coverage. Operator learning is newly discussed as an application, but no operator-learning experiment is reported.

E2.justification: Appendix A.11 adds primal parameter-space Gauss–Newton/Levenberg–Marquardt as an evaluated timing comparator; v1 discusses it theoretically without this empirical comparison. Adam, SGD, and L-BFGS remain the comparators in the original accuracy experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds two substantial evaluation designs: average iteration time over 500 optimizer iterations across residual/parameter-count grids, and PCG convergence across five landmark counts and six training checkpoints. These introduce controlled computational evaluations while preserving the original benchmarks' budgets, architectures, metrics, and settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.11 tests the computational regimes favoring primal or dual solves. Appendix A.12 adds a landmark-rank sensitivity study and Gramian-spectrum analysis across training stages, revealing insufficient-rank convergence failures. These analyses are absent from v1; the existing geodesic-acceleration comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten independent initializations, median benchmark errors, and interquartile bands in Figures 1–4. The additions introduce no new repeated-run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedure; averaging elapsed time over 500 iterations is a timing protocol.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Figures 1–4 retain their results. New Tables 9–11 report runtime comparisons, including 0.1681 seconds for primal versus 0.0078 for dual at m=300, n=18153. Table 12 newly reports 457 versus 31 PCG iterations at training epoch 450 for ranks 2500 versus 5000; Figure 5 adds spectral findings.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 adds explicit PCG cost and conditioning estimates, including O(t(mn+mℓ)) solve cost and an O(sqrt(κ_eff)) iteration estimate. Much of its dense/primal analysis restates existing costs. The formal definitions, primal–dual and geodesic propositions, and Appendix A.1 proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: residual-space natural-gradient training, inexpensive geodesic acceleration, scalable preconditioning, and accuracy at large parameter counts. The additional experiments support these retained claims without revising their headline scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds an applicability argument for physics-informed operator learning and explains the choice of standard tanh MLPs. Appendix A.12 also explicitly qualifies preconditioner effectiveness: insufficient landmark rank can prevent convergence, particularly later in training. The original benchmark discussion remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The additions document the timing sweep's A100 hardware, 500-iteration averaging procedure, and configuration grid, plus landmark counts and training checkpoints for the convergence analysis. Section 4.4 states the preconditioner construction/reuse schedule. Existing implementation algorithms and hyperparameter Tables 2–8 are retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to connect the method to push-through identities and kernel duality, earlier geodesic acceleration, and operator learning. New citations include Henderson and Searle, Benzing, Song, Bonfanti, Schwencke and Furtlehner, and Mckay, providing substantially more context for the contribution's relationship to prior methods.

P1.justification: v2 adds targeted related-work paragraphs, Section 4.4, an architecture rationale, and Appendices A.11–A.12. Existing section order and most prose remain unchanged. Publication-header, review-link, and bibliographic edits are limited presentation updates rather than a broad rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial diagnostic displays: paired timing grids, a color-coded primal/dual regime map, a six-panel spectral-evolution figure, and a rank-by-training-stage convergence table. Existing Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–8 retain their content and display structure, with page reflow and publication headers.

improvement.justification: Appendices A.11–A.12 provide useful direct evidence for computational advantages and preconditioner limitations that v1 mainly motivated theoretically. Expanded prior-work attribution and complexity discussion also improve context and practical guidance. The gains are focused: the new diagnostics cover a Navier–Stokes timing sweep and a cavity rank study, while the method and original accuracy evidence remain unchanged.
